source.check: Votes as printed in the Irish News block image (491-467=24, printed majority 24); the Belfast News-Letter OCR misprints 467 as 469, which would give 22. The result is marked 'Unionist gain'. Citation confirmed 6 Nov 2026: all surnames and most figures found in the page text.

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council, polled Thursday 2 June 1949 (Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1949: polling 'yesterday' for county and rural councils in Northern Ireland). The only county council contest was Newtownbutler; the Fermanagh Herald of 21 May 1949 reports that only one candidate was nominated in each of the other nineteen divisions and prints the whole nomination list, so all twenty members are recorded. Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it. M'Phillips was the Nationalist nominee (Belfast News-Letter, 19 May 1949), but no party label is printed beside his vote in the result.
